```{r}
# For mt = t^3
t = 1
for (t in 1:3){
  print((1/9)*(-1*(t-2)^3+4*(t-1)^3+3*t^3+4*(t+1)^3-1*(t+2)^3))
  t = t+1
}

# For mt = t^4

for (t in 1:3){
  print((1/9)*(-1*(t-2)^4+4*(t-1)^4+3*t^4+4*(t+1)^4-1*(t+2)^4))
  t = t+1
}

# For St = cos(2pit/3)
t = 1
for (t in 1:3){
  print((1/9)*(-1*cos(2*pi*(t-2)/3)+4*cos(2*pi*(t-1)/3)+3*cos(2*pi*t/3)+4*cos(2*pi*(t+1)/3)-1*cos(2*pi*(t+2)/3)))
  t = t+1
}
```

Question 2
```{r}
library(itsmr)

ts_deaths = ts(deaths, frequency = 12)
dec_deaths = decompose(ts_deaths, "additive")

# plot the result
plot(dec_deaths)

# plot the time series and the sum of the trend and seasonal components
plot.ts(ts_deaths,xlab = "Time", ylab = "Accidental Death Numbers in the U.S.")
lines(dec_deaths$trend+dec_deaths$seasonal, col = "red")

# plot the time plot of random noise
plot.ts(dec_deaths$random, xlab = "Time", ylab = "Random Noise")

# Plot the correlogram of the residuals
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.5, 2.1))
acf(na.omit(dec_deaths$random), lag.max = 71, ylim = c(-1, 1), main = "The Correlogram of Residuals")
```

```{r}
# Least Squares Estimation
t = time(deaths)
xt = lm(deaths~t+I(t^2)+cos(2*pi*t/12)+sin(2*pi*t/12)+cos(2*pi*t/6)+sin(2*pi*t/6)+cos(2*pi*t/4)+sin(2*pi*t/4))

# Plot the trend+seasonal component with the time series
ts_trend_seasonal = ts(predict(xt), frequency = 12)

plot.ts(ts_deaths, xlab = "Time", ylab = "Accidental Death Numbers in the U.S.")
lines(ts_trend_seasonal, col="red")

# Plot the time plot of residuals
yt = ts(resid(xt))

plot.ts(yt, xlab = "Time", ylab = "Random Residual")

# Plot the correlogram of the residuals
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.5, 2.1))
acf(yt, lag.max=71, ylim=c(-1,1), main = "The Correlogram of Residuals")
```

Question 4
```{r}
library(fpp3)

price = ts(prices$wheat, frequency = 1)

# Plot the time series of wheat price
plot.ts(price, xlab = "Time", ylab = "Annual Prices for Wheat in British Pounds")

# Plot the correlogram of the wheat price
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.5, 2.1))
acf(na.omit(price), lag.max = 30, ylim=c(-1, 1), main = "The Correlogram of Wheat Prices in British Pounds")

# Lag = 1, 2, 3, 4
TT1 = length(price)

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(price[2:TT1]~price[1:(TT1-1)], ylab = "Wheat Price", xlab = "Wheat Price in the Pevious Year")
plot(price[3:TT1]~price[1:(TT1-2)], ylab = "Wheat Price", xlab = "Wheat Price in Two Years Ago")
plot(price[4:TT1]~price[1:(TT1-3)], ylab = "Wheat Price", xlab = "Wheat Price in Three Years Ago")
plot(price[5:TT1]~price[1:(TT1-4)], ylab = "Wheat Price", xlab = "Wheat Price in Four Years Ago")
```

```{r}
bank = ts(bank_calls$Calls, frequency = 12)

i=1
my_list = list("")
for (i in 1:164){
  new_element = aggregate.ts(ts(bank[(1+(169*(i-1))):(169*i-13)], frequency = 12), nfrequency = 1)
  new_element2 = aggregate.ts(ts(bank[(157+(169*(i-1))):(169*i)], frequency = 13), nfrequency = 1)
  append(my_list, new_element, after = length(my_list))
  append(my_list, new_element2, after = length(my_list))
}

# Aggregation
bank_aggre = aggregate.ts(bank, nfrequency = 1)

# Plot the time series within the first 30 days
plot.ts(bank_aggre[1:420], ylab = "Aggregate Calls")

# Plot the correlogram of the aggregate calls
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.3, 2.1))
acf(bank_aggre, lag.max = 50, ylim=c(-1, 1), main = "The Correlogram of Aggregate Calls")

# Lag = 7, 14, 21, 28
TT2 = length(bank_aggre)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(bank_aggre[8:TT2]~bank_aggre[1:(TT2-7)], ylab = "Calls at t", xlab = "Calls t-7")
plot(bank_aggre[15:TT2]~bank_aggre[1:(TT2-14)], ylab = "Calls at t", xlab = "Calls t-14")
plot(bank_aggre[22:TT2]~bank_aggre[1:(TT2-21)], ylab = "Calls at t", xlab = "Calls t-21")
plot(bank_aggre[29:TT2]~bank_aggre[1:(TT2-28)], ylab = "Calls at t", xlab = "Calls t-28")
```
